docs.title: AnyDisasterMapping
docs.text: A unified satellite disaster-mapping framework covering the full lifecycle of crisis response with Earth observation: benchmark datasets, model zoo, training, inference, and deployment — companion to the survey Earth Observation for Disaster Mapping: Benchmarks, Methods, Challenges and Future Perspectives (SSRN 6725082).

docs.title: What's inside
docs.text:
Asset Count Where Task contracts 3 — seg, cd, scd src/tasks/ Registered models 34 src/core/registry.py Registered datasets 24 src/core/registry.py Ready-to-run configs 628 YAML configs/ Colab notebooks 17 (all auto-run, Drive-aware) repo root Disaster domains 13 docs/domains/

One config drives everything — model, dataset, augmentation, training and test loops are shared across all three tasks:

pip install -e . -c constraints.txt          # verified-good dependency set
python train.py --config configs/flood/urbanflood/seg_unet.yaml
python test.py  --exp_path results/<run> --checkpoint best.pth

docs.title: One-click Colab
docs.text:
Every notebook auto-runs top-to-bottom, mounts Google Drive, degrades gracefully to synthetic data when a dataset or checkpoint is unavailable, and never blocks on user input.

Notebook Purpose quickstart_colab.ipynb 5-minute end-to-end tour demo_colab.ipynb / demo_gif_colab.ipynb inference + animated output flood_ / wildfire_ / tsunami_ / hurricane_ / landslide_ / volcano_colab.ipynb per-domain pipelines change_detection_colab.ipynb bi-temporal cd task scd_colab.ipynb semantic change detection + transition matrix satellite_finetune_colab.ipynb fine-tune on your own imagery batch_inference_colab.ipynb large-tile / multi-scene sweeps ai_images_colab.ipynb generated-imagery stress tests dataset_download_colab.ipynb access hub for all 24 benchmarks checkpoint_zoo_colab.ipynb real weights → real inference (34-model zoo) evaluation_metrics_colab.ipynb OA / mIoU / F1 / confusion matrices

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: Trained models leave the framework through tools/export_onnx.py (ONNX opset 18 + TorchScript, onnxruntime-parity checked), the Dockerfile (CPU + --target demo Gradio image), or the Gradio app in gradio_demo/. See Tools & Deployment for the full guide.

docs.title: Provenance & QA
docs.text: This distribution includes the independent engineering review's remediation (FIXES_APPLIED.md): all blockers fixed, 58/58 registry imports tested in CI, full CPU smoke suite green (scripts/smoke_test_all_domains.py).

docs.title: Additional Disaster Domains — Extension Catalog
docs.text:
Beyond the 9 domains shipped in this extension (oil spills, avalanches, volcanic eruptions, tsunami inundation, hurricane/cyclone surge, glacial lake outburst floods, dust storms, wildfire smoke plumes, locust outbreaks), this catalog lists 21 further disaster types that can be added with the same adapter pattern. Each entry maps to one of the existing task contracts (seg / cd / scd) — no new task handlers are required.

Feasibility tiers: - Tier A — public pixel masks exist; drop-in addition (an adapter + configs + prep README, following docs/EXTENSION_GUIDE.md) - Tier B — labels derivable with a prep script; moderate work - Tier C — research-grade only; scarce masks, listed for roadmap completeness

docs.title: How to add one
docs.text:
1. Follow docs/EXTENSION_GUIDE.md: write an adapter in src/datasets/ that returns the exact tuple for its task contract (channel-first numpy, 255=ignore).
  2. Register it in src/core/registry.py (dataset_libs, lazy import).
  3. Add 2 configs under configs/<domain>/<dataset>/ (1 lightweight + 1 modern).
  4. Add scripts/data_prep/<domain>/README.md + make_dummy.py; extend scripts/smoke_test_all_domains.py.
  5. Run the smoke test — the whole loop is proven by make_dummy.py before any real data is downloaded.

Recommended Phase-2 order: #10 earthquake → #12 calving fronts → #14 algal blooms → #11 tornado → #13 coastal erosion (all Tier A; each ≈ one focused session).

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• Runtime Flow
  • Registries And Tasks
  • Config-Driven Build
  • Training And Evaluation
  • Practical Notes

docs.title: Runtime Flow
docs.text:
• train.py loads YAML through Config, applies CLI overrides, optionally sets resume, and calls Trainer.train().
  • test.py loads config.yaml from --exp_path or an override config, sets config.resume to the requested checkpoint, and calls Trainer.evaluate().
  • Trainer owns the runtime: model build, optimizer, scheduler, task handler, datasets, dataloaders, training loop, evaluation, and checkpointing.

docs.title: Registries And Tasks
docs.text:
• src/core/registry.py registers datasets and models through lazy_import(...).
  • DUAL_INPUT_MODELS describes named dual-input forwards and optional dual_head behavior for CD models.
  • DEEP_SUPERVISION_MODELS describes multi-output models such as DSIFN and UNet++.
  • src/tasks/__init__.py registers task handlers for seg, cd, and scd.
  • Task handlers define batch unpacking, model invocation, loss composition, prediction extraction, metrics, sliding-window evaluation, and augmentation target syncing.

docs.title: Config-Driven Build
docs.text:
• Models come from model.name plus model.kwargs.
  • Datasets come from dataset.name plus split-specific blocks under dataset.train, dataset.val, and dataset.test.
  • Trainer flattens nested dataset kwargs, and injects task or dataset.input only when the dataset constructor accepts them.
  • Augmentations are built from augmentation.train / augmentation.val; synced targets come from the task handler, not the dataset class.

docs.title: Training And Evaluation``
docs.text:
• The scheduler is built lazily in train() because some schedulers need len(train_loader).
  • Training has three main branches:
  • built-in loss via model_has_builtin_loss: true
  • deep supervision via DEEP_SUPERVISION_MODELS
  • standard task-driven loss via the task handler
  • best.pth stores weights only. latest.pth stores model, optimizer, scheduler, epoch/iteration, best metric, and early-stopping state.
  • Trainer.evaluate() switches to sliding-window mode when inference.sliding_kernel is set.
  • test.py also supports --test_splits, saving per-split metrics and a confusion-matrix-based aggregate.

docs.title: Practical Notes
docs.text:
• If the main validation metric is not mIoU, set training.metric_for_best_model explicitly.
  • Model kwargs are not fully standardized across wrappers. Use the wrapper __init__ signature as the source of truth.
  • The shared runtime contract is stable; reported upstream performance is not guaranteed without separate experiment validation.

docs.title: Data versioning — DVC pipeline + Zenodo DOI
docs.text: The 24 registered benchmarks are gated by their providers' licenses, so the framework ships adapters + access instructions rather than the bytes. This page describes how to version whichever subset you actually use, with bit-exact reproducibility.

docs.title: 1. DVC pipeline (dvc.yaml)
docs.text:
Three stages model the canonical flow — data preparation, training, testing — per domain config:

pip install dvc                      # one-time, or add to dev extras
dvc repro                            # runs only what changed
dvc status                           # drift check

Stages (see dvc.yaml at the repo root; defaults run the GLOF domain on synthetic dummy data via scripts/data_prep/glof/make_dummy.py — change the vars: block (config, data_dir, run_dir, epochs) for your own domain):

  1. make_data — runs the domain's scripts/data_prep/<domain>/make_dummy.py or your licensed adapter download; tracks the prepared split files (train.txt / val.txt / test.txt) and dvc.out the data dir.
  2. train — python train.py --config <yaml>; outs: results/<run>/.
  3. test — python test.py --exp_path results/<run> --force; metrics: results/<run>/test_metrics.json.

To add your own domain: override the vars: block (and the make_data cmd if you use a licensed adapter), then dvc repro. CI stays DVC-free (it uses the synthetic dummies), so adding stages never slows the pipeline down.

docs.title: 2. Storing the bytes — DVC remote
docs.text:
dvc remote add -d storage s3://your-bucket/anydisaster   # or ssh/, gdrive/, azure/
dvc push                                                 # upload data outs
dvc pull                                                 # restore anywhere

DVC writes .dvc pointer files (tiny, commit-ready) while the payloads live in the remote. Team members reproduce your exact data snapshot with git pull && dvc pull — no "which flood version was this?" again.

docs.title: 3. Public archival — Zenodo DOI
docs.text:
For citable, immutable releases (paper reviewer requirements etc.):

  1. Push the prepared dataset subset to a Zenodo deposit (or an open HF dataset repo, then mirror to Zenodo).
  2. Record the returned DOI in the domain doc (docs/domains/<domain>.md) and in the dataset adapter's access card (dataset_download_colab.ipynb).
  3. Tag the framework commit that consumed the dataset: git tag data/<dataset>-v1.0 <commit> so code + data versions stay paired.

Zenodo accepts files up to 50 GB each and mints a versioned DOI per release; combined with the sha256 manifests the framework already emits for checkpoints (export_manifest.json), any result in any paper can be traced back to exact input bytes.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• What To Register
  • Dataset Contract
  • Model Contract
  • Task Contract
  • Example: second + changemamba_scd
  • Validation

docs.title: What To Register
docs.text:
• Register datasets and models in src/core/registry.py.
  • Register new tasks in src/tasks/__init__.py.
  • Add public YAML configs under configs/<domain>/... only when the path is ready to support users.

docs.title: Dataset Contract
docs.text:
Return the tuple expected by the task:

  • seg: (image, label, sample_id)
  • cd: (pre, post, label, sample_id) or xBD-style (pre, post, loc_label, label, sample_id)
  • scd: (pre, post, cd_label, t1_label, t2_label, sample_id)

Current datasets usually return channel-first NumPy arrays plus integer labels; tensors are created later by the dataloader/task handler path. If the dataset uses albumentations, keep its masks aligned with the task handler’s augmentation_targets().

Some datasets also use dataset.input; the trainer passes that block as input_cfg when the dataset constructor accepts it.

docs.title: Model Contract
docs.text:
• Add the wrapper under src/models/ and register it in model_libs.
  • If it needs named dual-input forwarding, add an entry to DUAL_INPUT_MODELS.
  • If it returns localisation/classification heads separately, set dual_head: true there as well.
  • If it uses deep supervision, add an entry to DEEP_SUPERVISION_MODELS.
  • If the model computes its own loss, configs must set model_has_builtin_loss: true.

Model kwargs are not fully standardized across this repo. Use the wrapper __init__ signature as the source of truth.

docs.title: Task Contract
docs.text:
A new task usually needs:

  • unpack_batch
  • run_model
  • compute_loss
  • extract_predictions
  • _create_metrics
  • augmentation_targets
  • optional evaluate_sliding

If an existing task already matches your tuple and metric contract, reuse it instead of creating a new one.

docs.title: Example: second + changemamba_scd
docs.text:
This is a code-aligned example of how the current SCD path fits together:

IMPORTANT: this example is only a wiring example for the current runtime contracts. It has not been validated here as a reproduction recipe, and it should not be read as a claim that the repository reproduces the original reported second + changemamba_scd performance.

  • dataset.name: second maps to src.datasets.second.SECONDDataset
  • task: scd maps to src.tasks.scd.TaskSCD
  • model.name: changemamba_scd maps to src.models.ChangeMamba.ChangeMambaSCD
  • DUAL_INPUT_MODELS["changemamba_scd"] tells the trainer to call the model with pre_data= and post_data=

SECONDDataset returns (pre, post, cd_label, t1_label, t2_label, id), ChangeMambaSCD returns (output_cd, output_t1, output_t2), and TaskSCD supplies the matching loss and metrics. SECOND semantic labels use 0..6, so num_classes for the semantic heads and SCD metrics is 7, not 6.

There is no retained public configs/second/*.yaml in the current tree. The snippet below is only a minimal starting point.

task: scd
num_classes: 7
ignore_index: 255
model:
  name: changemamba_scd
  kwargs:
    output_cd: 2
    output_clf: 7
    in_chans: 3
    pretrained: pretrained_weight/vssm_tiny_0230_ckpt_epoch_262.pth
    backbone: vssm_tiny_224_0229flex
dataset:
  name: second
  train:
    dataset_path: data/SECOND/train
    data_list_path: data/SECOND/train.txt
    split: train
  val:
    dataset_path: data/SECOND/test
    data_list_path: data/SECOND/test.txt
    split: val
  test:
    dataset_path: data/SECOND/test
    data_list_path: data/SECOND/test.txt
    split: test
training:
  metric_for_best_model: Sek
  train_batch_size: 8
  eval_batch_size: 1
  num_workers: 4
output_dir: ./results/second/changemamba_scd

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• python train.py --help
  • python test.py --help
  • parse the YAML with Config.from_yaml(...)
  • import the registered dataset and model with the exact registry names you plan to use
  • run the smallest relevant regression or smoke check before large experiments

docs.title: Tools & Deployment
docs.text: Everything in tools/ plus the container and demo app — the bridge from a trained experiment to a deployed product.

docs.title: 1. ONNX / TorchScript export — tools/export_onnx.py
docs.text:
Builds the model through the same registry path the trainer uses, loads your checkpoint, and traces the forward pass exactly as the task handlers invoke it (seg: single image; cd/scd: dual inputs — DUAL_INPUT_MODELS kwargs call or channel-concat, per src/tasks/*.py).

# from a trained experiment dir (config.yaml + best.pth)
python tools/export_onnx.py --exp_path results/<run> --torchscript --check

# architecture check with random weights (no checkpoint needed)
python tools/export_onnx.py --config configs/oil_spill/oilspill_sar/cd_bit.yaml
flag meaning --exp_path export from a trained run (loads config.yaml + checkpoint) --config export from a YAML only (random weights) --size square input size, default 256 --opset ONNX opset, default 18 (17 down-conversion is lossy in onnxscript) --dynamic try dynamic batch/H/W axes; falls back to static when the architecture can't support it (honest, never hard-fails) --torchscript also trace model.torchscript.pt --check verify with onnxruntime: shape match + max abs diff vs PyTorch

Outputs land in exports/<name>/ with export_manifest.json (shapes, byte sizes, SHA-256). Extras: pip install -e ".[export]".

docs.title: 2. Pretrained weights — tools/download_weights.py
docs.text:
python tools/download_weights.py --list                  # what is published
python tools/download_weights.py --model unet            # one model
python tools/download_weights.py --model bit --task cd   # task-prefixed layout

Pulls from SyedRafiAhmedGIS/AnyDisasterMapping-weights on the Hugging Face Hub (flat <model>.pth or seg/ cd/ scd/-prefixed — same layout checkpoint_zoo_colab.ipynb consumes). Until the release is published the tool explains the fallbacks (train a config, or the zoo notebook's in-session tiny training) instead of failing.

Behaviour worth knowing:

  • --model unet prefers the flat root file; if only task-prefixed variants exist it asks you to add --task rather than guessing.
  • --all keeps the repo layout under --dest (seg/unet.pth, cd/unet.pth, …) so same-named files never overwrite each other; --all --task cd downloads only that folder.
  • Every download prints its SHA-256. A SHA256SUMS file in the release is verified automatically; --expect-sha256 <hex> pins one file; --revision <commit> pins the whole repo to an exact commit.
  • Exit code is non-zero on any failed/unverifiable download or when nothing matches; "release not published yet" is the only graceful 0.

docs.title: Checkpoint safety
docs.text:
All checkpoint reads go through src/utils/safe_load.py (torch.load(weights_only=True)). A file that needs full unpickling (e.g. older MAE/SatMAE releases embedding argparse.Namespace) is refused by default. If you trust the source, opt in explicitly:

ANYDISASTER_TRUST_CHECKPOINTS=1 python train.py --config <yaml>

docs.title: 3. Gradio demo — gradio_demo/app.py
docs.text:
Browser inference UI: upload imagery, pick a registered model, overlay the prediction. Runs standalone (pip install gradio>=4.0 pillow numpy imageio scikit-image) or via Docker:

docker build -t anydisaster-demo --target demo .
docker run --rm -p 7860:7860 anydisaster-demo    # → http://localhost:7860
# (the demo image sets GRADIO_SERVER_NAME=0.0.0.0; outside Docker it binds to 127.0.0.1)

docs.title: 4. Docker
docs.text:
Single Dockerfile, two targets, dependency layer cached against constraints.txt:

docker build -t anydisaster .                    # CPU/GPU training image
docker run --rm --gpus all anydisaster \
    python scripts/smoke_test_all_domains.py     # verify GPU stack
docker run --rm --gpus all \
    -v "$PWD/data":/workspace/data -v "$PWD/results":/workspace/results \
    anydisaster python train.py --config configs/flood/urbanflood/seg_unet.yaml

docs.title: 5. Dataset versioning — DVC + Zenodo
docs.text: dvc.yaml pins the make-data → train → test pipeline; docs/DATA_VERSIONING.md walks through pushing a DVC remote and minting a Zenodo DOI for the dataset snapshot.

Debris runs break the smooth snow signature with rough, darker material along slide paths. Spring imagery with stable snow lines works best for change-based verification.

docs.title: Run it in 3 steps
docs.text:
1. Open the notebook with the badge above (or from the README index).
  2. Runtime ▸ Run all — setup, a labeled synthetic sample, inference, dashboard and export chain automatically.
  3. Click 📤 to upload your own scene(s) — the inline preview shows exactly which files fit, and the pipeline re-runs on them automatically.

docs.title: Upload checklist
docs.text:
• Accepted: .png .jpg .jpeg .tif .tiff .h5 — GeoTIFF georeference is kept when present.
  • Sweet spot: 512–2048 px per side, ≤ 20 MB per file, pre/post pairs from the same area.
  • Set the GSD (m/px) box so km² statistics match your sensor (Sentinel-2 ≈ 10 m/px).
  • No imagery at hand? The 🛟 button generates an AI-style synthetic avalanche scene — clearly labeled, never presented as real data.

docs.title: Honest-results policy
docs.text: Every output is stamped with the mode that produced it — CHECKPOINT (your .pth), QUICK-TRAIN (genuinely briefly-trained) or SYNTHETIC-DEMO (clearly-labeled heuristic). Train your own checkpoint in satellite_finetune_colab.ipynb and upgrade any domain to CHECKPOINT mode.
